Heavy rainfall and flash flooding occurred overnight and this 
morning across Guam. This rainfall event was associated with the 
passage of Invest 95W, which remains a weak disturbance now east of 
the Marianas. Additional scattered showers and isolated
thunderstorms will be possible across Guam tonight. Drier conditions 
are seen across the CNMI, but a few showers and brief downpours will 
be possible.

As Invest 95W exits the region, drier conditions are expected 
through the rest of the weekend and through much of next week. Winds 
will be light and variable through much of next week. Model Time- 
Heights do show a shallow moisture setup through the first half of 
the week across the Marianas. Relative Humidity values look to fall 
to 30 percent around 700mb. This should help put a lid on potential 
island-effect days this week. Towards the middle and latter portions
of the week, moisture will return to the region with winds forecast 
to remain light through the atmosphere on Wednesday, which could 
allow for some island-effect showers. At this time, shower coverage 
remains isolated due to uncertainty in the quality of moisture depth.

Long range guidance continues to hint at a disturbance approaching 
the region next weekend. At this time, uncertainty remains high on 
any potential solution due to no trackable disturbance and a time 
frame that is 6 to 8 days out. As we continue to monitor the 
situation, it is important to emphasize that October is within peak 
typhoon season in the western Pacific. Residents in the Marianas 
should continue to monitor forecasts over the next several days, and 
maintain a general state of preparedness.

Marine...
Combined seas are between 5 and 8 feet across the Marianas. Seas are 
expected to fall over the coming days as the sources for both the 
primary long period northeast swell, and the secondary southwest 
well will weaken over the coming days. Surf will remain moderate 
across all reefs through at least Sunday night. A general downward 
trend in surf is expected over the next couple of days. 

Hydrology...
A Flash Flood Watch is in effect until 6 AM ChST Sunday morning for 
Guam. Widespread 2 to 5 inches of rain have fallen across Guam 
today. After a brief lull this afternoon, additional showers have 
developed leading to additional minor flooding. Flash flooding will 
remain a concern through tonight due to saturated soils across the 
island. Shower coverage will be widely scattered to scattered, but 
any shower will be capable of heavy rainfall. 

Tropical Systems...
At 100 PM ChST, Typhoon Koguma was located 255 miles southwest of 
Minamitorishima near 22N151E, moving west-northwest at 18 mph. 
Maximum sustained winds were 125 mph. Conditions remain favorable 
for further strengthening for the next 24 hours. Koguma is expected 
to make a turn toward the northwest Sunday and more north Monday. TY 
Koguma looks to remain over open ocean and is not expected to affect 
the islands of the Marianas or Micronesia.

For more information on TY Koguma, see bulletins issued by the Joint
Typhoon Warning Center (JTWC) under WMO header WTPN33 PGTW and by 
the National Weather Service under WMO header WTPQ33 PGUM.

A weak tropical disturbance, Invest 95W, is found along the monsoon
trough, and was centered west-southwest of Guam near 13N142E, moving
east-northeast. 95W is currently rated low, meaning development is 
unlikely during the next 24 hours. Scattered to numerous showers 
associated with 95W are found west of the center over Guam and 
adjacent coastal waters. At best, conditions are marginal for 
development, with weak outflow aloft and moderate vertical shear. 
models are in very good agreement that Invest 95W will not become a 
significant tropical cyclone. Invest 95W is expected to move east- 
northeast over the next few days with little change to slight 
weakening as it progresses. 

For more information on Invest 95W, see bulletins issued by JTWC
under WMO header ABPW10 PGTW. 

Eastern Micronesia...
The monsoon trough is making itself known across the Marshall 
Islands today. Latest satellite data shows cloudy skies with 
numerous showers across the Marshalls this afternoon. Although 
thunderstorms have not really been seen so far, the potential for a 
few does exist, so maintained thunder in the forecast. The monsoon 
trough looks to break away from TY Koguma, reorienting back south 
over eastern Micronesia. This will help maintain convection across 
the Marshalls, while allowing the showers and thunderstorms to drift 
farther south over Pohnpei and Kosrae. Yesterday's model runs 
indicated the effects of the monsoon trough would remain north of 
Kosrae, with the island only seeing low-end scattered showers. this

showers and thunderstorms than Pohnpei. Either way, the dry pattern
